newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical rests case in breast implant suit.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical rests case in breast implant suit.

text.p: Defendant Dow Chemical Co. rested its case in a breast-implant class-action suit Monday, and closing arguments were set for Thursday.
The trial, in which women are seeking damages for what they say are illnesses related to the silicone implants they received, began March 27.

The implants were manufactured by now-bankrupt Dow Corning Inc., a joint venture of Dow Chemical and Corning Inc.. The suit claims that Dow Chemical was liable because it allegedly tested silicone compounds in its laboratories for the joint venture and withheld evidence that they could be harmful.
This was the first implant class-action case against the chemical giant to go to trial.

Dow spokesman John Musser said the company was "extremely satisfied" with how the trial had gone. "We think we've made a very strong argument that Dow Chemical did nothing to harm these women," he told Reuters.
State District Judge Yada Magee told the jury to return to the court Thursday morning for closing arguments.
